messages:
ana: Noticed odd quota churn in console for a couple tenants after the client releases this morning. Burns hop between 'standard' and 'fast-path'.
josh: Any logs showing why attribution jumped? Could be header differences.
maria: Quick grep of edge shows the TS runtime now emits `X-Route-Intent: fast` on retry attempts. That header is being treated as a distinct route in telemetry.
ana: (typo) ana: oops
josh: So retries generate events that look like separate routes -> sampling/order causes dashboard to attribute to different buckets.
ingest-bot: Alert: quota-attribution-anomaly created (ID QAA-2026-03). Linked to current console spike.
qa: Short-term mitigation idea: normalize attribution at ingest by sticky-ing to the first seen route for token+trace for 3m. Low-risk flag.
maria: Agreed for immediate relief. Medium-term: change SDKs to send non-attributing intent header `X-Client-Intent` instead of `X-Route-Intent` on retries.
josh: Also consider making routing policy ignore route-hint on retries so behavior is consistent across clients. That needs design review.
ana: Can we add a metric that counts how often we normalized attribution? Need to ensure we're not hiding legitimate route switches.
ingest-bot: Deploy queued: console/ingest/telemetry-normalizer -> canary us-east-1.
maria: I'll open TS PR to switch header and add config `retryRouteHint=false` default in next patch. Will notify release notes.
ana: After canary, run the quota smoke test (burst + retry flood) and post results here. QA will sign off before broad roll.
josh: Thanks all. I'll monitor dashboards during canary and keep support in the loop. :thumbsup:
